updates.title: Dashboard tiles load quickly and one slow tile does not hold up the others
preconds: Sign in on the build under test as an Admin user. Admin holds every permission, including Reports, so Reports and Dashboard both show in the top menu.
In the top bar choose the busiest location you can reach (the one with the most invoices and clocked time), so every tile has real work to do.
Have a stopwatch or a phone timer ready.
steps: Click Work Orders in the top menu so you start away from the Dashboard.
Start the stopwatch and click Dashboard in the top menu.
Stop the stopwatch when all six tiles (Revenue, Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency, Technician Utilization, Sales by Customer, At Risk Customers) show a figure.
Write down the time.
On each of the four top tiles and on Sales by Customer, click the range pill and choose Last 12 Months.
Watch the tiles while each one reloads and note whether any tile stays blank or waits for another tile.
Repeat steps 1 to 4 two more times and write down each time.
results: Each time, all six tiles show their figures in about one second. A load that clearly takes several seconds, again and again, is reported.
The tiles fill in on their own: no tile waits for another tile before it shows its figure.

This part cannot be checked by hand: the measured targets (95 of every 100 first loads within 1 second, each tile's server time within 250 ms, no single query over 500 ms, and a 2-second cut-off that fails only the slow tile). Write "targets not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see.
Making one tile slow or fail on purpose is not possible by hand. Write "slow-tile cut-off not checked by hand" in the result comment.

↳ Finance tab > Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment dialog opens, close it without taking a payment. Do not send or pay the invoice.

notes: The task brief says v42 notes that reversal is how a void is made. v42 has no such sentence (the words "reverse" and "reversal" do not appear in it). The tech plan, section 7, says the opposite: "the invoice factory's reverse() does not void an invoice — it hard-deletes it", and a voided invoice is made by adding a line to an already-invoiced work order whose invoice is still pending. So C88632, C88635 and C88642 use both routes: Reverse (the invoice is removed) and the add-a-line-to-an-unpaid-invoice route (a real void). C88643 and C88645 use Reverse only. The observable expectation (contributes nothing) is the same for both.

No UI route is known for an invoice with no company (no customer). A work order needs a customer. C88632, C88635 and C88642 ask the tester to try a Part Sale without a customer and otherwise to write "no-customer invoice not reachable by hand". The PRD context note under S5-E3 says QA should expect to create the case rather than find it: PO/dev question, how is one created by hand?

The PRD does not say which New Line field is "invoiced hours" (labor time billed) and which is "invoiced technician hours" (technician time recorded on lines). The cases read Tech Time as invoiced technician hours. The Billing Efficiency cases set Estimated Time equal to Tech Time so they do not depend on the answer, and tell the tester to mark Blocked if Advisor Analysis Hrs Invoiced does not match.

Credits are issued through Issue Credit, which the playbook records as a parts-only picker ("Parts to return", Outcome Store Credit / Refund). So every credit in C88633 and C88634 is made by returning a part.

Shop supplies and the Parts / Labor split: the PRD does not say which side shop supplies fall on. C88636 tells the tester to set the customer's Default Shop Supplies to 0 where shown, and to mark Blocked if shop supplies alone change the split. Candidate PO question.
Negative money format is not specified. The Sales report design shows "$-422.01". C88634 asks the tester to record the format and not judge where the minus sign sits.
Rounding of row sums against the supporting-line totals is not specified (C88650). The tester marks Blocked with both numbers if they are 0.01 apart.
Chart tooltips in the design show whole percentages (e.g. "Marcus Halvorsen 117%") while the reports show two decimals. C88649 compares after rounding.

Report naming: the PRD says "Service Advisor Analysis report". The design's report menu item reads "Advisor Analysis" and the page title reads "Service Advisor Analysis". The cases use both. Tech plan NFR-010 says "Labor Efficiency %", but the design's Service Advisor Analysis column reads "Billing Efficiency". C88632 refers to the on-screen column.

Exact clocked hours depend on editing the clock record (work order three dots > Timesheets (n), or Reports > Timesheet Activities). Every case gives the fallback: use the real hours shown and adjust the arithmetic.
